t:
(a) Designation.—Not later than 30 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the United States Board on Geographic Names (referred to in this Act as the “Board”) shall designate the unnamed, 13,895-foot peak in the Alaska Range in Denali National Park and Preserve in the State of Alaska, located at latitude 62.920469308 and longitude –151.066510314, as the “Mount Stevens”. 
    (b) References.—Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the peak referred to in subsection (a) shall be deemed to be a reference to the “Mount Stevens”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "Board" signals an advisory body with outside members, as in the examples involving commissions and advisory boards. But the United States Board on Geographic Names is a federal interagency body, and Congress simply directs it to name the peak, with no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any non-federal party. Subsection (b) is only a boilerplate references clause.
fable.s: the United States Board on Geographic Names (referred to in this Act as the “Board”) shall designate the unnamed, 13,895-foot peak

opus.w: The section tells a federal body, the U.S. Board on Geographic Names, to name a peak and says how federal records should refer to it. It involves no consultation, comment period, hearing, advisory panel with outside members, or right to sue for anyone outside the federal government. The word "Board" might suggest outside involvement, but this Board is a federal entity acting on a direct order from Congress, so everything stays inside the government.
opus.s: the United States Board on Geographic Names (referred to in this Act as the “Board”) shall designate the unnamed, 13,895-foot peak in the Alaska Range in Denali National Park and Preserve in the State of Alaska
opus.b: **Tempting reading:** the United States Board on Geographic Names is a "Board," so it could look like an advisory body that brings in outside input. That reading fails. The Board is a federal body inside the executive branch. Here it is simply told to designate a name within a deadline. No one outside the federal government is consulted, there is no hearing or comment period, and no outside party gets a right to object or sue.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the United States Board on Geographic Names, a federal agency, to designate a mountain name. The Board is part of the federal government, and its actions are internal administrative decisions. There is no requirement for consultation with state governments, the public, or other non-federal entities before this designation is made.
qwen_chat.s: the United States Board on Geographic Names (referred to in this Act as the “Board”) shall designate the unnamed, 13,895-foot peak in the Alaska Range in Denali National Park and Preserve in the State of Alaska, located at latitude 62.920469308 and longitude –151.066510314, as the “Mount Stevens”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "United States Board on Geographic Names" is an advisory body involving outside experts, and thus its designation constitutes participation. However, the Board is a federal agency (part of the USGS/Interior Department), and its members are federal employees or appointed officials acting in an official capacity. The definition states that Congress, federal agencies, and federal officials are INSIDE the federal government. Therefore, a decision made by a federal board is an internal government action, not participation with outsiders.
